meta.description: Request a report, park at zero tokens on a machine wait gate until a file-based signal lands, then verify independently. A machine timeout is a failure, never an approval.

graph.name: report-and-verify
graph.description: File-handoff review behind a MACHINE WAIT GATE - the canonical until_argv exemplar of the starter set. No run_context seeds: everything parameterized rides the handoff files. THE MACHINE-GATE LAW this graph encodes: (1) a gate with wait:{until_argv,every_s,timeout_s} parks the run at ZERO tokens, re-running a check until it exits 0; (2) until_argv is FIXED argv - never a shell string, never a pipeline; (3) {run.KEY} renders into goals, contexts, fan-out goals and gate QUESTIONS but NOT into until_argv - a placeholder left in argv reaches the machine as a literal token and dies 'program not found' forever, so parameterized data crosses on FILES, not in argv; (4) timeout_s expiration FAILS the gate with the last probe output as its answer - the run never proceeds on silence, machine timeout is failure not approval; (5) exit 0 releases once. HANDOFF CONTRACT (the producer side is outside this graph - any cron job, peer agent, or human): ROOT = ${WF_RAV_ROOT:-$HERMES_HOME/wf-report-verify}; read ROOT/request.json; write the answer to ROOT/report.md; then write the exact string 'ok' to ROOT/ready. The probe reads those fixed names under ROOT resolved from the ENVIRONMENT, which is what keeps argv fixed and the dispatch parameter-free. NODE MAP: prepare (fresh ROOT, writes request.json, clears stale signals) -> await-report (machine gate, polls every 30s, fails the run at 900s) -> verify (independent reader: checks report.md against the request's requirements; the producer's prose is not evidence). Retarget by editing the ask text below or pointing WF_RAV_ROOT at a staging root for tests. A cron scheduler may double-dispatch: give the launch a lane_key if that matters to you.

defaults.context: You are one lane of a report hand-off. Ground rules: touch only the agreed handoff root; never fabricate the producer's answer; every judgement cites the bytes you read; keep the answer to the schema; one fenced json block as the final message; never print secrets.

nodes.goal: Open the report handoff. ROOT = ${WF_RAV_ROOT:-$HERMES_HOME/wf-report-verify} (resolve it with your shell; do not invent a different path - the machine gate and the producer both read exactly this). 1) mkdir -p ROOT. 2) Delete stale signals: ROOT/ready and ROOT/report.md (a leftover ready marker would release the gate on a PREVIOUS lap's content). 3) Write ROOT/request.json containing exactly this request as valid json: {"ask": "What changed since the last report, and what is still broken?", "requirements": ["answer both parts of the ask", "stay under 200 lines", "cite concrete paths or commands for every breakage"], "protocol": "write the answer to report.md, then write the exact string ok to ready"}. 4) Read request.json back and check it parses. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"root": "<resolved ROOT>", "request_path": "<ROOT/request.json>", "stale_cleared": <true only if both files were removed or never existed>}

nodes.context: Machine gate - no human question. Parked until the producer writes ROOT/report.md and a ROOT/ready file containing ok. Timeout at 900s FAILS this run; that is the design (a missing report is a failure, not an approval).

until_argv:
import os,sys,pathlib
R=pathlib.Path(os.environ['WF_RAV_ROOT']) if os.environ.get('WF_RAV_ROOT') else pathlib.Path(os.environ.get('HERMES_HOME') or '~/.hermes').expanduser()/'wf-report-verify'
try:
    r=(R/'ready').read_text().strip()
    b=(R/'report.md').read_text()
except OSError as e:
    print('not-ready: '+type(e).__name__, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)
if r=='ok' and b.strip():
    print('report-and-verify: released, report.md '+str(len(b.encode('utf-8')))+' bytes')
    sys.exit(0)
print('report-and-verify: signal invalid (ready=%r, report bytes=%d)'%(r[:20], len(b.strip())), file=sys.stderr)
sys.exit(1)

nodes.goal: The wait gate released - ROOT/report.md exists and ROOT/ready said ok (prepare's committed answer names ROOT). Now JUDGE the report as an independent reader: read ROOT/request.json and ROOT/report.md yourself. Check EVERY requirement in the request against the actual bytes (both parts answered, length limit honored, breakages cite concrete paths). A release signal proves the file landed, nothing more - the producer grading itself is not evidence. verified=true only when no requirement fails; failed_requirements names each miss with the requirement it missed. report_excerpt: the report's own first ~15 lines, verbatim. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verified": <bool>, "failed_requirements": ["<requirement: what missed>"], "report_excerpt": "<verbatim excerpt>"}
